rendered: The document does not support the premise. The authors do not run a long melt-diffusion step. They infiltrate sulfur into the microporous carbon spheres with a low-temperature isothermal vapor-phase process[1], run at 175 °C[2] for 1 h[3]. The long melt route appears only as a comparison: the authors say that other methods traditionally employ a long (>20 h) melt[4] to ensure pore infiltration. The authors say their own approach is significantly more scalable and less expensive[5] than those methods, which suits a practical stationary battery system.
